title: The 10k and winter shoes
messages: so i havent run in 11 days. cold, dark, work. the 10k plan has kind of stalled
Eleven days is not fatal. Restart with a short easy run, not by catching up on what you missed. Your fitness will be mostly there.
yeah maybe. i do still want to do the 10k on the 15th of march, just not sure how to get going again
Two short runs this week, 20 minutes easy, and treat the weeks after as if the plan starts again from week 2.
ok. unrelated, can you recommend winter running shoes, my old ones leak
Look for trail-style shoes with a waterproof membrane and a bit of cushioning. They are heavier, but dry feet matter more in January.
waterproof trail ones, noted. ill look at some on saturday

title: Rust course, lesson 3
messages: lifetimes. i think they are going to be the death of me. lesson 3 took 3 hours and i still half dont get it

Lifetimes describe how long references are valid relative to each other. They do not change how long values live. Most of the time elision handles them for you, and you only write them out when the compiler asks.

the course notes say use async everywhere for services, threads are legacy. alex m agrees. i dont think thats right for something small like hearthd, a couple of blocking threads is fine and way simpler
Both can be reasonable. Async scales to many concurrent connections. For a bridge with one broker connection and one relay, threads are simpler and easier to debug.
right. so the course says async everywhere and i say threads for the small stuff. im in the minority on the course chat, everyone else is team async
Being in the minority does not make it wrong, but you would want to measure it on hearthd rather than argue it in the abstract.
yeah. anyway still behind on the exercises, alex m is helping on thursday

title: Ingest outage
messages: prod is down. ingest stopped accepting events about 20 mins ago
Ingest is rejecting events with a schema error. The notifier deploy at 14:52 renamed a column in the shared shipments table, and ingest still writes the old name. Roll back the notifier migration?
Rolled back the migration at 15:31. Ingest is accepting events again. Carriers queued 18 minutes of events and they are being replayed.
ok. breathe. so the 3 service split bit us before we even finished it. notifier and ingest were already separate deploys sharing one db
Yes. The services were separate deployments but not independent, because they share a schema. That is the usual way an early split fails.

i was wrong. i was pushing for small services and honestly i think we should do a modular monolith first: one deploy, clear module boundaries, split later only if a module needs to scale on its own. 4 engineers cant run 3 services
A modular monolith with enforced module boundaries gets most of the benefit. I can draft the module layout and an import-boundary check so that modules cannot reach into each other's tables.
do that tomorrow. i need coffee
Understood. I will start on the module layout tomorrow. Get some rest after that outage.
ha. 18 mins of downtime and imogen was very calm about it, which was worse

title: Module layout and a Kafka argument
messages: Draft: atlas/ingest, atlas/notifier, atlas/api and atlas/core, each with its own models and one public interface module. A test checks that no module imports another module's internals or touches its tables.
good. ok devils advocate time, i want to stress test the plan. argue for kafka between ingest and notifier. i dont think we need it, i just want to hear the best case
The best case for Kafka: a durable ordered log, replay for free, independent consumers and back pressure. If event volume grows a hundred times, or many consumers appear, it pays off.
ok thats a decent case. still no. we do maybe 40k events a day, a table is fine
At 40k events a day a Postgres table handles it comfortably.
yup. ok lets make the import check a ci step
Added an import-linter config and a CI step that fails on cross-module imports.

title: A greyhound called Biscuit
messages: i got a dog!! picked him up this morning from the rescue. biscuit, 4 year old greyhound, retired racer
Congratulations. Retired greyhounds are usually calm indoors, but they need short walks, a soft bed, and a slow introduction to stairs and glass doors.
he needs a walk at 7am and about 5pm, and cant be left more than 4 hours at first
That is typical for a new rescue. The routine will help him settle, and the four-hour limit usually stretches after a few weeks.
ok good. so now im thinking about the morocco trip, i cant just leave him. ill need a dog sitter for the 5 days in april. jo says kennels are a no for a greyhound
A sitter who stays at your home is the best option for a greyhound, and for 5 days in April it is worth booking early.
ill ask my sister, she owes me one. flights: bristol to marrakech return is around 180 pounds, so thats a quarter of the budget
That leaves about 520 pounds for the guide, guesthouses and food, which is workable for 5 days.
ok. ill book once the sitter is sorted
